Stella Lefty Faces Fourth Plagiarism Allegation Over ‘Misery’ And The Greatest Showman

By

Simran Pasricha

Published

September 8, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:23
Instaread

Stella Lefty is facing a fourth round of plagiarism allegations and this time it seems she may have dipped into the musical theatre world, allegedly of course! Listeners have begun comparing her song “Misery” to The Greatest Showman track “A Million Dreams”.

 

The debate began brewing in YouTube comments before taking off on social media over the weekend. No legal claim has been publicly reported, and a listener comparison is of course not proof that a song was copied. Still, people have been putting their headphones on, opening several tabs and entering their investigative journalism eras with Lefty’s music. Here’s a look at the songs that have prompted the comparisons so far.

Did Stella Lefty copy “Boston” from Noah Kahan?

The first major comparison centred on “Boston”, Lefty’s breakout hit. Listeners heard similarities with Noah Kahan’s “Stick Season”, and Kahan is now credited as a co-writer on Lefty’s track. Reports said Kahan’s team contacted Lefty’s camp before the song’s official release.

Lefty addressed the situation in a Vanity Fair interview, saying, “When I was writing the song, I wasn’t thinking about Noah Kahan. I was literally thinking about nothing at all.”

She continued: “I don’t want to step on anybody’s toes, so I’m like, if this sounds like that, whatever, all good.”

Fans have since combed through Lefty’s socials finding several videos of her covering “Stick Season” on her TikTok.

Did Stella Lefty copy “Summer You Were Mine” from The Chicks?

Next up was “Summer You Were Mine”, which fans noticed contained similarities to The Chicks’ 1998 song “There’s Your Trouble”.

This case has a clearer explanation. The song was an approved interpolation, meaning it reworks a recognisable element of an existing song rather than directly sampling its recording. The Chicks songwriters Tia Sillers and Mark Selby were initially absent from streaming credits, but Lefty’s label Atlantic Records told Rolling Stone that this was due to a “streaming platform error”. Their names have since been added.

However, some comments think that Lefty’s release is actually similar to another song —  “Soak Up the Sun” by Sheryl Crowe, but this is all speculation thus far.

Did Stella Lefty copy “Why Wouldn’t We” from Blake Shelton?

Then came “Why Wouldn’t We”, from Lefty’s album Long Way Home. Listeners compared it with` Blake Shelton’s 2017 single “I’ll Name The Dogs”, pointing to similarities in melody and lyrics about sharing the domestic load in a relationship.

One TikTok commenter wrote, “Honestly it’s not just the melody, even the lyrics are essentially the same.”

Neither Shelton nor the song’s writers, Matt Dragstrem, Ben Hayslip and Josh Thompson, have publicly addressed the comparison since reports emerged. They are also not credited on “Why Wouldn’t We”, which lists Lefty, Emily Weisband, Grady Block and Steph Jones as writers.

Did Stella Lefty copy “Misery” from The Greatest Showman?

Now, listeners are comparing “Misery” with “A Million Dreams”. One TikTok comment responding to the side-by-side clips read: “Jesus this is worse than the ‘Stick Season’ one”.

“Misery” is credited to Lefty, Madi Yanofsky and Phil Cook. “A Million Dreams” was written by Benj Pasek and Justin Paul, with Rob Mathes credited as arranger, none are currently listed on “Misery”.

For now, it remains another fan-led allegation. Whether anyone involved responds is another matter entirely.

PEDESTRIAN.TV has reached out to Stella Lefty for comment.

We’re Taking Over This Bondi Hot Spot For 2 Weeks, So Consider Your Sweet Treat Cravings Sorted

By Saacha Neilson

Brought to you by our mates at

Sydney, we’re hosting a Vitasoy pop-up so all you little treat lovers can check it out and finally join our Little Wins Collective. 

ICYMI, we’re running a Little Wins competition and asking people to submit the small everyday wins that can brighten each & every day. 

Rather than just leaving the little wins to the universe, we’re putting our money where our mouth is by hosting our own pop-up with Vitasoy, handing out plant-based drinks & snacks so our Sydney audience can seek out a sweet treat and find a little win for themselves. 

Sounds like your sort of activity? Keep on reading to make sure you don’t miss a moment. 

Give me the deets

We’re taking over North Bondi’s infamous gelato and matcha bar, Luca & Luca, from August 31 and running a two-week residency. 

Sweet treat seekers can order from a specialty Vitasoy menu. Not to mention, there’ll be unique postcards on offer as well as a dedicated Vitasoy fridge, fully stocked with free plant-based samples to be handed out every day. 

Luca & Luca is open from 3pm till late every Monday, 12pm till late from Tuesday to Friday, and from 11am on weekends.

How do I join the Little Wins Collective? 

In case you’ve been living under a rock, the Little Wins Collective is our movement that motivates everyday Aussies to share small wins in their daily lives that keep them going.

We’ve even created an interactive map for Melburnians and Sydneysiders to contribute to, so one little win can go on to improve any number of days. Experienced a little win recently? Simply head to our site and drop it in so your fellow city dwellers can head on down and get a win for themselves. 

A little win could be anything from a fave busker who makes your morning commute to, oh, I don’t know, a free Vitasoy yogurt at Luca & Luca. And with a $3K prize pool up for grabs, we’ve got our eyes peeled for only the best of the best to take out top spot. 

And even if you don’t win the comp, you’ll get to be part of a community celebrating the small stuff that makes life so sweet. Honestly, isn’t that the exact brand of positivity we all need these days? 

If you’re ready for a little win, head to Luca & Luca from August 31 to check out Vitasoy’s residency and put yourself on the map.
